messages:
maria (eng-platform): heads up — APAC privnet GPU onboarding is failing about 30% of the time since the keystore fence went live this morning. most failures show KMS timeouts and egress DENYs.
lee (eng-sre): :eyes: which nodes/az? any pattern by instance type or subnet?
maria (eng-platform): failures concentrated in ap-southeast-1b, warm-pool-3. instance type p4d.* and p4d.*-spot both hit. failures started immediately after the keystore rollout at 08:12.
deploy-bot: deploy "keystore-fence/v2" finished at 2025-07-02 08:12:17 UTC — trigger: rollout/keystore-fence.
olivia (eng-security): this was expected — we tightened privnet egress to only allow privatelink->keystore endpoints. did the keystore IP set update get propagated to that region?
sam (eng-infra): we pushed the endpoint CIDR list to apac at 08:10, but the firewall ruleset was applied at 08:11 via policy-service. should be in sync.
lee (eng-sre): logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts to the keystore proxy and then NAT gateway denying the conn because of missing flow rule. snippet:
```
2025-07-02T08:12:23Z kubelet: keystore: handshake failed: dial tcp 10.22.14.99:443: i/o timeout
firewall: drop conn src=10.22.14.99 dst=nel-keystore-apac-01 proto=6 action=DENY rule=egress-keystore-v2
```
maria (eng-platform): customer onboarding flows are retrying and backpressuring the scheduler — we've got provisioning backlogs and increased cost because instances spin and fail. cc @carmen this touches onboarding SLAs.
carmen (customer-success): customers in APAC saw delays. one enterprise test suite timed out. we need a mitigation asap, they escalate if onboarding stalls > 15m.
olivia (eng-security): quick decision: either widen keystore egress CIDR for affected subnets OR create a temporary tag-based firewall exception for gpu-warm-pool nodes while we validate the keystore proxies. I'm leaning to tag exception for minimal blast radius.
sam (eng-infra): tag exception looks fastest. we can add rule: allow egress to keystore FQDN for resources tagged gpu:warm-pool=true for 2 hours. I'll prepare terraform change and a rollback timer.
lee (eng-sre): while infra works on the rule, we should add a local retry/backoff tweak to the onboarding controller to reduce churn. small patch to controller: increase backoff to 10s->60s and cap retries to 6. reduces repeated node churn.
maria (eng-platform): agree. i'll open a controller PR and mark it hotfix. sam — can you own the firewall change and the 2-hr TTL?
sam (eng-infra): on it. plan:
- push tf change to allow tag-based egress to keystore FQDNs (not CIDR)
- add policy-service flag to set automatic revoke at 2h
- notify ops when rule is live
ETA 30m.
olivia (eng-security): make sure rule is scoped to the exact tag and keystore domain names only — no broader egress. audit log retention for this rule must be set to 90d (we need the trail).
lee (eng-sre): i'll land the controller patch in 15m and roll to staging → prod canary on warm-pool-3. will coordinate with sam for traffic cutover.
carmen (customer-success): thanks — i'll notify affected customers about a short delay and that we have a mitigation in progress.
maria (eng-platform): action items: sam (firewall exception + TTL), lee (controller backoff patch + canary), olivia (audit retention & approve rule), maria (monitor and rollback plan). ping here when rule is live. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: policy change queued: PR #4821 by sam — awaiting review.
sam (eng-infra): PR merged, applying now. rule should be visible in 2–3m.
maria (eng-platform): seeing reduction in failures — current fail rate down to ~4% for new attempts. continuing to monitor.
olivia (eng-security): confirm audit logs are being emitted to central-logs and retention flagged.
sam (eng-infra): confirmed — logs in central-logs/keystore-egress/apac, retention=90d.
maria (eng-platform): thanks everyone. follow-up: we need a postmortem and a runbook update to include tag-exception workflow and keystore rollout checklist. i'll carve a small doc after stabilization.
lee (eng-sre): adding to postmortem: investigate why keystore proxy in apac had higher TLS handshake latency — could be connection tracking or NAT exhaustion.
olivia (eng-security): also we should consider a staged rollout for future keystore fences with canary subnets.
maria (eng-platform): agreed. closing thread when doc is up.
